title: Text requests can call tools and stream replies
summary:
The text API gained tools and streaming, then spent the rest of the week making those responses more predictable, while community-built apps kept arriving.

Completion requests gained `tools` and `tool_choice`, with tool calls preserved in OpenAI-compatible responses and function results accepted in follow-up messages. Requests using `stream: true` gained provider-backed server-sent events. Subsequent changes made chunks consistently readable as SSE and checked that streams end with one `[DONE]` event. Software found several ways to finish a stream; the API is aiming for one.

The OpenAI text request limit doubled to 512,000 message characters. The model list gained `openai-reasoning`, backed by o1-mini, and the `hypnosis-tracy` persona. SearchGPT also gained support for an explicitly selected model.

The text API moved several generators to a shared client and updated its Cloudflare chat completions integration. OpenAI-style responses retain existing IDs and timestamps; request fields and stream chunks are handled more consistently. Error handling was tightened so streaming API errors return HTTP errors, while the later overhaul preserved provider error details. OpenAI-backed routes also moved through a gateway client.

PrivatePollenAI joined the directory with local chat storage and Pollinations-powered text and images. Gacha joined the social bots list with chat, web search, and character-aware image generation; Musify joined the creative apps list with an AI music assistant, voice commands, and playlists. Directory links and creator attribution also got some maintenance.
